title: The Bosphorus Brief — Monday, 27 July 2026
overview: A quieter regional day: the US-Iran strike pause held for a second straight day, easing some of the anxiety that had gripped markets last week. At home, the central bank's rate decision and a national sporting title dominate headlines, while court and residency news carries the usual mix for foreign residents.
sections: <parameter name="heading">Money: Rates on hold, inflation forecasts rise
body: Turkey's central bank held its policy rate at 37 percent for a fourth straight meeting, with IntelliNews noting the expected cut was shelved amid the Iran war flare-up. Deutsche Bank has meanwhile raised its Turkey inflation forecast to 30 percent. For residents, this means continued high borrowing costs and no near-term relief on the lira, which sits at 47.33 to the dollar and 53.86 to the euro today. Budgeting for rent, tuition, and imported goods should assume this rate environment persists for now.
